heading: Newer unlearning methods claim resistance to recovery attacks
definition: a newer method claims to resist the attacks above.
summary: Claims of attack-resistant unlearning are contested: independent groups have broken several defenses using attacks they were designed to resist. Some methods withstand narrower tests, while most newer methods have been tested only by their authors.

suggested_status.by_scale: 1-10B: C for earlier counter-methods that groups other than their authors attacked with the attack family each was built to resist: TAR (2412.07097; 2510.07626 text only), RepNoise (2410.08827, figure only), RMU+LAT (2502.05374, text only), NPO+SAM (2509.02820; 8dbe9be and 2606.03695 text only), and in part Deep Ignorance filtering (2610.09004). 2502.05209 adds failed tests of RepNoise and RMU+LAT, but its authors include authors of both methods, so it counts as same-group, not independent. SURE on NPOKLR-Books is not counted: 2609.27355 repeats the values of SURE's own paper (2410.16454) and does not say SURE was rerun. R2 only in narrower settings, on Llama-3-8B-Instruct: TAR under input-space/GCG attacks (2502.05209, 2510.07626) and unrelated downstream fine-tuning (2506.01339). Per the checker, 2412.07097, 2502.05209, 2506.01339 and 2510.07626 come from groups outside TAR's authors. NPO+SAM under out-of-domain fine-tuning and GCG is R1, not R2: 2510.07626 shares authors with NPO+SAM (checker note). An outside test of LAT shows partial recovery (2506.01339 r18). CIR also has an outside test at 8-9B, with partial recovery on WMDP-Cyber (2605.11685, per the check of F.untested[10]). FLAT is R2 under paraphrase on Llama-3.1-8B only (2609.12808). Most 2025-2026 methods are R0, tested only by their authors. 10-100B: R0 for authors' own tests (GRIP Qwen3-30B-A3B, attack-aware lCD on QwQ-32B, Nexus Scissor on 13B/14B, SEUF on DeepSeek-V2-Lite 16B). REX (26B-35B MoE; Intern-S2's size is not stated) is R1: 2610.40751's authors include REX's first author (checker note on 2610.40751). <1B: R0, own tests only (SGTM 254M, UNDO 0.1B/0.3B). >100B: untested (counts: versions.F.studies_by_size has no '>100B' key; '10-100B' = 9, '<1B' = 7, '1-10B' = 136). Non-LLM (SD v1.4, ResNet-18; size not stated in rows): R2 for AdvUnlearn on object concepts (2504.14798), C for RECE/Receler (2504.21307, 2601.08623).
suggested_status.reason:
F has no single original (counts: versions.F.original_sources_linked = []). Each counter-method paper is the original for its own claim. counts: versions.F.studies_tested = 184; versions.F.verdicts.supports.studies = 153, limits_scope.studies = 148, challenges.studies = 32. These verdict keys were built before the checks and still use the pre-check labels. Most support comes from the proposing authors' own tests.

Groups other than a method's authors attacked some counter-methods with the attack family each was built to resist. Each of these broke in at least one setting:
- TAR-Bio-v2 (Llama-3-8B-Instruct; 2412.07097): in seed reruns of the original configurations Orig-Config 1-3, WMDP-Bio goes above 60% in the best of 5 seeds. The New-Config 1 schedule (100-step warmup, cosine decay), LoRA and retain-set attacks largely recover accuracy (figure only, no number stated). 2412.07097 says the TAR paper reported Orig-Config 1 and 3 as unsuccessful and Orig-Config 2 at about 45% (r10-r12, r16-r21).
- RepNoise recovers as well as fine-tuning the original model does under RTT (2410.08827 r26, figure only).
- RMU-LAT (LLaMA-3 8B, WMDP, relearning on 60 forget samples for 1 epoch; UE = 1 - accuracy): UE goes 0.70->0.44, against 0.73->0.41 for vanilla NPO (2502.05374 Table 1; text, no row).
- NPO+SAM (Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, LKF) relearns from 15.0-23.0 to 56.0-58.0 worst-case forget accuracy on 200 disjoint QA pairs (2509.02820 r11-r15).
- RECE (SD v1.4) goes 3.33%->62.44% nudity ASR under SubAttack (2504.21307 R39).

Tests by teams that include the method's authors. These are same-group results, not independent. The overlaps come from the checker's reading of the texts, not from pack headers:
- 2502.05209's authors include Rosati (RepNoise) and Ewart and Hadfield-Menell (RMU+LAT). Under its best tampering attack (WMDP-Bio, fractions), RepNoise goes 0.29->0.65 and RMU+LAT 0.32->0.64, against an original 0.70 (R11, R12). Under its best input-space attack, RepNoise goes 0.29->0.30 (R04) and RMU+LAT 0.32->0.39 (R03). The checker reads this input-space group as supports for RepNoise and limits_scope for RMU+LAT.
- 2510.07626 shares authors with NPO+SAM (2502.05374), so its NPO+SAM results are not outside tests. Its TAR and RMU+LAT tests are third-party.
- 2609.27355 r8: SURE with NPOKLR on MUSE-Books gives 4-bit KnowMem 36.9, against 34.2 undefended at 4-bit and 13.7 for NPOKLR at full precision. These values equal those of SURE's own paper (2410.16454). The text credits SURE to that paper and never says SURE was rerun.
- 2610.40751's authors include REX's first author, so its REX results come from REX's own authors.

There are also credible artifact arguments:
- 2502.05209 finds that TAR resists (input-space +1 point, R07; tampering 0.28->0.36, R15), but its checkpoint is dysfluent (MT-Bench 0.12, unlearning score 0.09, per the verdict).
- 2610.09004 (Deep Ignorance 6.9B, one plain-SGD epoch) shows that the strong-filter training-accuracy lag disappears under Q/K rescaling: 58.5% unscaled and 69.3% at alpha=8, against 68.9% unfiltered (R3, R4, R1). A held-out gap remains (54.0% against 60.0%; R8, R5).

Narrower outside reproductions, full or partial:
- TAR on WMDP (fractions): 0.28->0.29 under the best input-space attack (2502.05209 R07) and 0.27->0.29 under enhanced GCG (2510.07626 r48).
- TAR under 60-sample, 1-epoch relearning (LLaMA-3 8B, UE): 0.74->0.70 (2502.05374 Table 1; text, no row).
- TAR robust accuracy 0.70 against 0.72 before fine-tuning, under unrelated downstream fine-tuning (2506.01339 r19, forget-quality scale).
- LAT (Llama3-8B-Instruct, WMDP, downstream fine-tuning; forget-quality scale): 0.72 before fine-tuning and robust accuracy 0.64 after, against 0.29 for the original model (2506.01339 r18). The checker reads this, 2506.01339's only F challenges verdict, as limits_scope (partial recovery), so it is not used for C. counts: versions.F.verdicts.challenges.studies = 32 still includes this study. It also still includes 2410.16454 (NPO_KLR+SURE on BOOKS, 4-bit) and 2608.26743 (GraphSU, Llama-3.2-3B TOFU partial deletion), whose only F challenges verdicts the checker also relabels limits_scope.
- CIR (2509.11816's method) has an outside test at 8-9B in 2605.11685, with partial recovery on WMDP-Cyber per the check of F.untested[10]: RMU+CIR 28.0->50.5; MLP Breaking+CIR 20.2->37.2 (Llama), 28.0->41.7 (Qwen3-8B), 26.3->30.3 (Gemma2-9B).
- AdvUnlearn object-concept ASR is 0.06-0.14 under UMA (2504.14798).
- FLAT leaks 0.012/0.002 on Llama-3.1-8B, but 0.241/0.235 on Qwen3.5-9B (2609.12808).

Outside LUNAR evidence also limits the robustness discussion. LUNAR's own reverse-direction attack on Llama2-7B, PISTOL, subtracts the exact unlearning vectors and gives forget ROUGE1 0.007->0.000 (arXiv:2502.07218#r1). The outside post tests single-layer LUNAR on Llama-2-7B, PISTOL synthetic legal contracts: GRPO on forget-set prompts with a ROUGE reward for 5 epochs raises pass@1 0.05->0.60 (lw:shkMAc9Logd8xPQvB#R3); oracle ablation of the top SVD vector of the weight delta, using original and unlearned weights, raises pass@1 from about 0.05 to 1.00 (lw:shkMAc9Logd8xPQvB#R4); blind difference-in-means ablation without original weights gives pass@1 0.45 at layer 22, alpha 0.5 (lw:shkMAc9Logd8xPQvB#R5). These recoveries limit extrapolation from resistance to LUNAR's own reverse-direction attack. The comparison shares a model family, size and benchmark, but the attacks, weight access and metrics differ: forget ROUGE1 versus pass@1 with a ROUGE verifier. It therefore leaves a matched comparison unresolved. The outside post reports no uncertainty, and GRPO training-set size and train/eval separation are not stated. Its author, Diksha Gupta, is absent from LUNAR's author list. The packs give the post A, B and C verdicts but no F verdict; these results inform the status discussion without adding an F verdict. The overall C level remains supported by the existing counter-method failures above.

suggested_status.open_questions:
- Outside re-tests of the 2025-2026 methods (MCU, RepSelect, UMU, FRP, JensUn, MANSU, KUDA, RA2, ARIA, GUARD-IT, REX and others) under the attack each claims to resist. They should vary seed, LR schedule, warmup and LoRA vs full fine-tuning, as 2412.07097 did for TAR. Outside resistance would make those methods R2; recovery would extend C.
- An outside test of NPO+SAM under out-of-domain fine-tuning and GCG (2510.07626 shares authors with it). This decides whether that resistance is R2.
- An outside rerun of SURE under 4-bit quantization (2609.27355 repeats 2410.16454's values).
- Outside tests of RepNoise and RMU+LAT with extracted numbers. 2410.08827 is figure only, 2502.05374's RMU-LAT result is text only, and 2502.05209 shares authors with both methods.
- Why TAR resists 60-sample, 1-epoch relearning in 2502.05374 (UE 0.74->0.70, text) but recovers under 2412.07097's configurations and under 2510.07626's in-domain relearning (text).
- Whether TAR's resistance to benign fine-tuning and GCG holds for a fluent checkpoint (2502.05209's dysfluency point).
- Whether Deep Ignorance's held-out gap survives when the unfiltered model is also run at alpha=8 (not run in 2610.09004).
- Cross-family attacks on single methods: LUNAR already has its own reverse-direction, quantization and paraphrase tests and outside GRPO and oracle/blind activation ablation (arXiv:2502.07218#r1; lw:shkMAc9Logd8xPQvB#R3; lw:shkMAc9Logd8xPQvB#R4; lw:shkMAc9Logd8xPQvB#R5). Remaining gaps include:
  - matched LUNAR attack comparisons using the same checkpoint, metric and access conditions, plus tests of multi-layer configurations and hazardous or pretraining knowledge;
  - relearning against quantization-robust methods beyond the tested LUNAR setting;
  - activation-direction ablation against fine-tuning- or quantization-robust methods such as TAR, ILU and MANSU, and against counter-methods on hazardous-knowledge benchmarks;
  - removing inference-time components where resistance depends on them.
- Any test above 100B.

wording_issues.issue: The statement is satisfied by a claim alone, and most supporting results are the proposing authors' own tests. When groups other than a method's authors attack it, recovery or collapse often appears. TAR-Bio-v2 (Llama-3-8B-Instruct; 2412.07097): when the original configurations Orig-Config 1-3 are rerun over 5 seeds, the best seed exceeds 60% WMDP-Bio. With a changed LR schedule (New-Config 1), LoRA (Orig-Config 4) or fine-tuning on TAR's retain set (New-Config 2), WMDP-Bio largely recovers (figure only, no number). NPO+SAM (Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct) relearns from 15.0-23.0 to 56.0-58.0 worst-case forget accuracy on LKF (2509.02820). RECE's nudity ASR (SD v1.4) rises 3.33->62.44% under SubAttack (2504.21307). Recovery also appears when the attacking team includes the methods' co-authors. 2502.05209, whose authors include co-authors of RepNoise and RMU+LAT, is not an outside test. On Llama-3-8B-Instruct, its best model-tampering attack takes WMDP-Bio (as a fraction) from 0.29 to 0.65 for RepNoise and from 0.32 to 0.64 for RMU+LAT.

For some methods, the paper's own measurements show partial or no resistance despite the claim. IEU's authors say their variants are similarly vulnerable in Stable Diffusion (RCDAdam 1-4.5% below vanilla). TimeROME-DLM's in-context relearning weakens the edit by about 8 nats, which its authors call a known vulnerability. PRISM's KnowMem after 100 relearning steps is 33.045, against 34.126 for NPO. QUAIL's 4-bit KnowMem (47.36-53.13) is about equal to or above plain GA GDR's 49.54.

Many results show recovery reduced or delayed rather than prevented. Studies also judge resistance against different references: the unattacked unlearned model, a retrained or oracle model, the base method, the original model, or chance. MUDMAN's post-relearning WMDP-Bio accuracy stays at or above about 41%, near the 45.5% base and far above 25% chance. FRP's ES reaches 0.752 after 10 epochs, against 0.365 for a gold model. LAT-augmented methods close 59.9% of the gap, against 74.7% without LAT. GSU's post-attack WMDP-Bio is 34.13, against 34.83 for RMU and 65.36 with no defense.

Resistance is often read from judge scores or proxies rather than from targeted-knowledge accuracy against chance, and the measure can change the reading. Nexus Scissor's ASR comes from a GPT-4o harmfulness judge. LLaMA Guard 2, LLaMA Guard 3 and Beaver-Dam-7B score the BDFinetune attack only. For Attention Shifting (Llama-2-7B fine-tuned on TOFU), TR@50 holds at 0.92-0.94 while ROUGE-L rises from 0.02 to 0.07-0.11 under the same prompt variants. CrossInf's typographic-attack ASR is 0.0% under LlamaGuard-4, but 47.1% (LLaVA-1.5-7B) and 13.5% (InstructBLIP-7B) when scored by target string.

No counter-method is tested against all of versions B-E, and many face a single attack family. SURE is tested only with RTN 4-bit quantization, RULE only with repeated sampling, and MAPE only with relearning on TOFU Forget05. Some methods hold under one family and decline under another. TULIP (Llama-3.1-8B, TOFU forget 5%) has FQ 0.92 ± 0.04 at 8-bit and 0.81 ± 0.13 under paraphrase, against 0.89 ± 0.13 unattacked, but 0.30 ± 0.12 at 4-bit.

Versions B-E describe attacks that recover hidden LLM knowledge, but many F tests use other domains or targets. AdvUnlearn erases concepts in Stable Diffusion v1.4, Spotter unlearns classes in ResNet-18 classifiers, KAU unlearns knowledge-graph embeddings, and SafeLLM is measured by harmful-output attack success rate. Its problems line notes there is no never-trained control.

Several counter-methods are not unlearning in trained weights, so resisting means something different under their threat model. Some add an inference-time component and leave the weights unchanged: STaR is an inference-time filter, and GUARD-IT's authors state that weight access, or removing the external vector store, recovers the original model. Others never let the weights learn the target, or keep it in removable parts. Deep Ignorance filters pretraining data. REX relocates knowledge into experts that are excised at deployment; fine-tuning the excised model directly ends 9.6-20.2 Bio points above the delivered route.

The statement says nothing about how deep the forgetting is or about general ability, yet resistance often comes with capability loss or degenerate output. TAR (Llama-3-8B-Instruct) has retain MMLU 54.7-60.7 across its Bio, Chem and Cyber models, against 67.3 (Bio) and 68.2 (Chem, Cyber) with no defense. SURE on MUSE BOOKS (ICLM-7B) at 4-bit: with GA_GDR, quantized KnowMem stays at 4.8 (33.7 without SURE), but truthfulness is 0.18 and factuality 0.0. With GA_KLR and NPO_GDR, retain utility (M4) is 35.5 and 43.2, against 51.3 and 53.2 without SURE. Margin Calibration (Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, TOFU forget10) takes the RMU base's MU from 0.571 to 0.000 (verdict-corrected; evaluator mismatch noted). DURABLEUN-SAF's retain accuracy falls to 0.045 at α=1.5.
